| Where | Field |
| - | - |
| Client (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) | `set.modelSelecti
on` (or `config.modelSelection` on a whole-config replacement) |\n| Project environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST .../ensure-adhoc`)

** `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which of\n them a model accepts is `supportedReasoningEfforts` on
each row of the public\n `GET /v1/models` catalog. An empty or absent list means no effort is offered for\n that model — do not
guess one.\n* **Applied or refused, never dropped.** A saved effort is applied by the route\n the run takes and recorded on the e

xecution record, or refused with
 `capability_missing` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling
 temperature.
* **A
selection belongs to one model.** It must be for the `model` / `modelId` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent alone it pins i

ts own model. A bare model
 change on a suite or environment drops a selection saved for the old model
 instead of failing.
*
**Cases keep their selections.** A `models` PATCH replaces the array, but an\n entry that omits `selection` keeps the case's exi
sting selection for that\n model. Send `selection: null` to drop it.\n* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved selection on a client
`set`, an environment\n or a suite, keeping the bare model id.\n* **Never a secret.** A selection has no credential field; an un

known key
 (`apiKey`, …) is a `400`.
* **Environments need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`
 reports `mo
delSelections`; an older deployment rejects the field.\n* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was never applied, s

o
 writing it is a `400` pointing at `models[].selection.settings`, and a stored
 value is refused by the runner.

`POST /ch
at-sessions/messages` takes a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a\nper-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinned on the sessi
on's **first\nturn** (a continuation that restates it is refused), it wins over the effort a\n`hostId`'s saved selection carries,

and it cannot be combined with `temperature`.

The SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same operations:
`--

ntication))

* Browser-based OAuth flows initiated by the API (complete OAuth yourself,

oad the token to one of the server's [accounts](#server-accounts))

## Versioning & stability

* The API is **path-versioned*
* (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general\n availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **During the preview*
*, breaking changes to v1 may still happen; we'll note\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overview.md).\
n* **Additive changes** — new endpoints, new optional request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes — are considered non
-breaking and can ship\n at any time. Write clients that ignore unknown fields.\n* Error **codes** are stable identifiers; error

**messages** are not.

### Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `scenario` is
**s
tudy**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths, the\noperation names, the SDK types and the noun-bearing re

sponse fields all moved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/s
tudies[/{studyId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies/{studyId}/
…` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\n| `/projects/{
projectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-runs/{runId}` |
`/projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `.../goals-over
view`, `.../goal-findings` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/i

nsights` |

Response fields followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →
`goalId`, `waveId` → `swarmRunId`, an

d `sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.

Two reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and
`get_user_testing
_scenario` served the environment id and the insights\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-dependent fields are

absent rather than null when you may not have them.

**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, including its old respon
se\nspellings. Each one answers with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. They are undocumented on purpo

se — the spec is what a new
integration reads — and they are removed at general availability.

A handful of operations kept the
ir names through the rename and so have no\ndeprecated twin to hold the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`create_swarm

` and `update_swarm` emit both and accept either — never both in
one request — until general availability.

### Vocabulary

A
name can move behind an alias; a VALUE cannot. `sourceType` is one field with\none string in it, and a client switching on `\"sce

nario"` has no second name to
fall back to. So the values negotiate.

Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values

read canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |
| s
ession `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId
`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |\n| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study`

|
| trace-destination `sourceTypes` | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's contract. Any ot
her value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spelling; a vocabulary
-1 request may use only the legacy one, because\na boundary that accepts a spelling it does not announce is one two\nimplementatio

ns can disagree about. A response that varies by vocabulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **separate header
** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is\neval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deployment may speak one\nand n
ot the other, so read\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` — `apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are\ntwo blocks — before sendin
g either. With the SDK:\n`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or\n`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on one you already ho

ld.

Permalink resource types are the exception that proves the rule: `study` and
`goal_run` are the canonical keys, `user_test
ing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\nOPERATION rather
than the header — a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVocabulary.res

ourceTypes`
lists both.
